title: How search finds the page you mean
material:
# How our docs search finds the page you mean

Type "reset my password" into our docs search and the first result is a page called "Account recovery". The two share no words. This is how the search gets there.

## Matching words is where search started

The classic approach splits the question into words and looks each one up in an index: a list of every page that contains it. Pages that share more of the question's words, and rarer words, score higher. It is fast and it is exact, and it fails when the page you need uses different words.

## Meaning as a position

We run every passage through an embedding model, which turns a piece of text into a list of 384 numbers. Those numbers work like coordinates: passages that mean similar things land close together, whatever words they use. We embed each passage ahead of time, when the docs are indexed, and the question at the moment you ask.

## Finding the nearest without measuring everything

Comparing the question with every passage costs one comparison each, which is too slow as the docs grow. So the index links every passage to its closest neighbours, with a few long links that cross the whole map (the structure is called HNSW). A search hops from neighbour to neighbour and checks a small share of the passages.

## Keeping the exact matches

Meaning search is weaker on exact things such as product names and error codes, so we keep the word matches as well. The two ranked lists are merged by position: a page near the top of both lists moves up the most. Last, a slower model re-reads the question together with each of the top few results and moves the best one to first place.

rows.label: The one idea
rows.text: Search finds the page you mean by comparing where meanings sit, not which words match.

rows.label: The gap it closes
rows.text: You type what you want in your own words, and cannot see how search finds a page that shares none of them.

rows.label: Who it is for
rows.text: Developers who use a docs search and know what an index is, but not how meaning is compared.

rows.label: A · Follow the question
rows.text: The query “reset my password” travels through every stage of the search until it comes back as the page “Account recovery”.
rows.detail: A worked example, as a trip through one world: the search is one long set and each chapter is a stop. Every chapter does something to the query, so every beat has the same thing to point at.

rows.label: B · The map of meaning
rows.text: One map of every passage in the docs. Each chapter adds a layer to it.
rows.detail: One diagram that grows, in one frame that keeps rebuilding. It suits chapters 2 and 3, but matching words and re-reading don't happen on a map.

rows.label: C · Two searches
rows.text: The same query typed into the old search and the new one, side by side.
rows.detail: Before and after, as a split screen that collapses to one. It shows that the new search wins, not how it works.

rows.label: Open
rows.title: The question
rows.asks: You typed “reset my password”. The page is called “Account recovery”. How did search find it?
rows.ends: The mismatch is on screen: not one word in common.
rows.shape: A question, asked with the real input
rows.covers: The question only: the three words typed and the page that answers them. No mechanism yet.
rows.cue: Key clicks, then a rising tone
rows.first: You type three words into a docs search.

rows.label: Chapter 1
rows.title: Matching words
rows.asks: Why can't search just match the words?
rows.ends: Word matching puts “Password policy” first and never sees the right page.
rows.turn: The ranked list comes back with “Password policy” on top, and “Account recovery” is not on it at all.
rows.shape: The naive version, then where it breaks
rows.covers: Keyword search: splitting the question into words, the index of pages by word, and the ranked list that misses “Account recovery”.
rows.cue: The pulse thins, then drops out
rows.handoff: The query chip leaves the search box, as a chip in flight and arrives above the word index, where it splits into three words: one camera follows it; no cut.

rows.label: Chapter 2
rows.title: Meaning as a position
rows.asks: If not words, what can search compare?
rows.ends: On a map of meaning, the question lands next to “Account recovery”.
rows.covers: Embeddings: text into numbers, numbers as a position, and the docs placed on the same map ahead of time.
rows.cue: A pad lifts, with a chime on the join
rows.handoff: The query chip leaves the failed list, re-formed from its three words and arrives at the mouth of the model that turns text into numbers: the list drops away under it; no cut.

rows.label: Chapter 3
rows.title: Finding the nearest, fast
rows.asks: With thousands of passages, how does it find the nearest one quickly?
rows.ends: Hopping along links between neighbours reaches the nearest passages in a few steps.
rows.covers: Finding the nearest passages: why measuring every distance is slow, and the web of neighbours that makes it a few hops.
rows.handoff: The query dot leaves the close-up with its neighbour and arrives as one dot among thousands on the whole map: the dot stays put while the camera pulls back; no cut.

rows.label: Chapter 4
rows.title: Two lists, one answer
rows.asks: Exact words still matter sometimes. Can search keep both?
rows.ends: Merged and re-read, the list puts “Account recovery” first.
rows.covers: Hybrid search: keeping the word list beside the meaning list, merging them by position, and re-reading the best few.
rows.handoff: The five lit passages leaves the map, as dots and arrives as the rows of a second list: the dots fly out and stack while the map falls away.

rows.label: Close
rows.title: The answer
rows.asks: What comes back to the search box?
rows.ends: The page you meant, open at its line, and the idea in one sentence.
rows.shape: The result, then the route in one line
rows.covers: The answer back in the search box, and the idea restated on it. No new mechanism.
rows.handoff: The top row, “Account recovery” leaves the re-read list and arrives as the first result under the search box from the opening: the camera pulls back until the list is the real results; no cut.
rows.last: Search doesn't look for your words. It looks for your meaning, nearby.

rows.label: Voice
rows.text: One calm narrator, at about 90 words a minute.

rows.label: Music
rows.text: A quiet pulse under the voice. It thins when word matching fails, lifts on the map and resolves on the answer.

rows.label: Look
rows.text: Paper and ink, with one green kept for the query.

rows.label: Returning picture
rows.text: The map of meaning, which chapters 2 and 3 share.

beats.title: The mismatch
beats.takeaway: The words you typed aren't in the page that answers you.
beats.focal: the query in the search box
beats.change: The query is typed and the top result rises under it. A scan looks for words they share, and none light up.
beats.result: Query and title side by side, with no shared word marked.
beats.enters: semantic handoff: the film opens here

beats.title: The question
beats.takeaway: Something other than matching words found that page.
beats.focal: the query chip lifting out of the box
beats.change: The results fall back, and the query lifts out of the box as a chip and sets off into the search itself.
beats.result: The chip is in flight and the search box is behind it.

beats.title: An index of words
beats.takeaway: Classic search looks up each word in an index of the pages that contain it.
beats.focal: the index: each word with its pages
beats.change: The chip splits into its three words. Each word drops onto its row in the index, and the pages on that row light up.
beats.result: Two rows are lit: “password” with three pages and “reset” with two. “my” is greyed out.
beats.claim: c1. The page names in the index are illustrative (i1).

beats.title: Rank by matches
beats.takeaway: Pages are ranked by how well their words match, so a page with your words wins.
beats.change: The lit pages leave the index, form a list and sort by score. “Password policy” climbs to the top.

beats.title: Where it breaks
beats.takeaway: The right page shares no words with the question, so word matching can't see it.
beats.focal: the “Account recovery” page, outside the list
beats.change: The camera travels down past the end of the list and finds “Account recovery” unlit. Its text is scanned against the three words and nothing lights.
beats.result: The right page sits outside the list, tagged “0 words in common”.

beats.title: Text becomes numbers
beats.takeaway: A model turns any piece of text into a long list of numbers.
beats.focal: the model the chip passes through
beats.change: The chip goes into the model. A row of numbers comes out the other side and keeps unrolling while a counter runs up to 384.
beats.result: The question is now a row of 384 numbers.
beats.leaves: the query, as a row of numbers

beats.title: Numbers are a position
beats.takeaway: Those numbers are coordinates: they put the text at one point in a space.
beats.change: The row of numbers folds into two axes, with a note that this is 2 of 384 dimensions. The row shrinks to one dot at its position.
beats.result: One labelled dot on an empty map.
beats.enters: the query, as a row of numbers
beats.claim: c5. The flat map is a simplification, and the picture says so.

beats.title: The docs are already there
beats.takeaway: Every passage of the docs was put on the same map ahead of time, and similar meanings sit close together.
beats.change: Passages from the docs stream through the same model and land as dots. They gather into groups, and a label lands on each group.
beats.result: A full map with three labelled groups.
beats.claim: c6. The count of 12,000 is illustrative (i1).

beats.title: Next to its answer
beats.takeaway: The question sits right beside the passage that answers it, though they share no words.
beats.focal: the query dot and its nearest neighbour
beats.change: The camera pushes in on the query dot. The nearest dot lights and opens into its passage. A line joins the two and a similarity value lands on it.
beats.result: The question and the “Account recovery” passage, joined by a short line marked 0.83.

beats.title: Checking everything is slow
beats.takeaway: Measuring the distance to every passage works, but it gets slow as the docs grow.
beats.change: The camera pulls back to the whole map. The query dot draws a line to every other dot, one after another, while a counter races up.
beats.result: The map is covered in lines and the counter reads 12,000.

beats.title: A web of neighbours
beats.takeaway: Ahead of time, each passage is linked to its nearest neighbours, with a few long links that cross the map.
beats.change: The measuring lines clear. Short links grow between neighbouring dots, then a few long links arc across the map above them.
beats.result: The map is a web: short links everywhere, a few long ones on top.

beats.title: Hop towards the answer
beats.takeaway: The search hops along links, always to the neighbour closer to the question, and arrives in a few steps.
beats.focal: the ring that hops from dot to dot
beats.change: A ring starts on a far dot, takes a long link across the map, then shorter and shorter hops, each to the neighbour nearest the query. It stops on “Account recovery” and the five nearest passages light up.
beats.result: The ring is on “Account recovery”, five passages are lit, and the counter reads about 200.

beats.title: Keep both lists
beats.takeaway: Meaning can blur exact things like a name or an error code, so search keeps the word list too.
beats.focal: the two lists, side by side
beats.change: The five lit passages fly off the map and stack into a list. The word list from chapter 1 slides back in beside it, and a tag lands on each.
beats.result: Two ranked lists side by side, each tagged with what it is good at.

beats.title: Merge by position
beats.takeaway: The lists are merged by position: near the top of either list is good, near the top of both is best.
beats.focal: the merged list forming between them
beats.change: Rows from both lists slide to the centre. A page found in both joins into one row and jumps up. The merged list settles.

beats.title: Re-read the best few
beats.takeaway: A slower, more careful model reads the question against each of the top few and puts the best answer first.
beats.focal: the question held next to one passage at a time
beats.change: The query chip visits the top three rows in turn. Each passage opens beside it and gets a bar for how well it answers. The rows reorder and “Account recovery” moves to the top.
beats.enters: the query chip, with the merged list

beats.title: The page you meant
beats.takeaway: The search box shows the page you meant, opened at the line that answers you.
beats.focal: the first result in the search box
beats.change: The camera pulls back until the list is the results under the search box from the opening. “Account recovery” opens and the line that answers the question is highlighted.
beats.result: The opening frame again, now with the right page open at its line.
beats.leaves: the query, back in its box

beats.title: The idea
beats.takeaway: Search found it by comparing where meanings sit, then re-reading the best few.
demands: the route with its four stops
beats.change: The route the question took draws itself as one line with four stops, each lighting as it is named. The line then shortens into the last sentence.
beats.result: The last sentence alone on screen, held.
beats.enters: the query, back in its box
beats.leaves: semantic handoff: the film ends here
